scr_ar_resolving_errors.purpose: Explains how to resolve A/R import errors — reading the error file, correcting the rejected rows and re-importing only those rows so nothing is loaded twice.
scr_ar_resolving_errors.outcome: Every rejected customer or invoice row is corrected and loaded exactly once.
scr_ar_resolving_errors.rootCause: An A/R import is rarely clean on the first pass during a property takeover; if rejected rows are not worked back in, the opening aging silently understates what residents and tenants owe the new owner.
scr_ar_resolving_errors.ifSkipped: Rejected invoices never load, so opening A/R falls short of the seller's aging and the GL tie-out fails.
redFlags: Error files sitting unworked after go-live
Whole file re-imported instead of only failed rows, creating duplicates

scr_ar_import_error_notification.purpose: The notification RealPage sends when an A/R import finishes with errors, linking to the error file that lists each rejected row and the reason it failed.
scr_ar_import_error_notification.outcome: The importer is alerted immediately that part of the load failed.
scr_ar_import_error_notification.rootCause: Offline and automated imports run unattended; without a notification, a partially failed customer or invoice load looks successful and nobody reconciles the shortfall until an auditor or owner does.
scr_ar_import_error_notification.ifSkipped: Partial imports go unnoticed and receivables are understated for months.
redFlags: Notifications routed to a departed user's mailbox
Error notifications with no follow-up ticket

scr_ar_common_errors.purpose: Catalogues the most frequent A/R import errors — unknown customer IDs, inactive GL accounts, invalid dates, closed periods, mismatched entity/location codes — and how to prevent each.
scr_ar_common_errors.outcome: Import files built right the first time, cutting rework during onboarding.
scr_ar_common_errors.rootCause: Most A/R import rejections come from a handful of predictable mistakes; knowing them before loading a portfolio avoids days of back-and-forth during a management transition.
scr_ar_common_errors.ifSkipped: The same avoidable errors recur on every property takeover and delay the first close.
redFlags: Invoices dated into closed periods
Location codes that do not match the entity structure

scr_ar_handling_import_errors.purpose: Procedure for handling an A/R import that returned errors — downloading the error file, fixing source data, and confirming the corrected totals tie to the seller's aging.
scr_ar_handling_import_errors.outcome: A complete, reconciled A/R load after errors are worked.
scr_ar_handling_import_errors.rootCause: Fixing rows is not enough; the finished import must be proven complete by tying loaded invoice totals to the source aging, otherwise small losses of rows stay hidden inside a large balance.
scr_ar_handling_import_errors.ifSkipped: Loaded A/R never gets reconciled to the source aging and differences surface at audit.
redFlags: No signed tie-out of loaded A/R to source aging

scr_ar_a_r_and_payments.purpose: Chapter covering the A/R settings that affect payments across RealPage Accounting — payment configuration, A/R terms and account labels.
scr_ar_a_r_and_payments.outcome: A/R payment behaviour configured consistently for every entity.
scr_ar_a_r_and_payments.rootCause: Terms and labels drive due dates, discounts and the revenue accounts invoices hit; configuring them once and correctly prevents systematic misposting across the portfolio.
scr_ar_a_r_and_payments.ifSkipped: Due dates, discounts and revenue coding vary by user and aging is unreliable.
redFlags: Terms set up differently per property with no rationale

scr_ar_about_accounts_receivable_and_pay.purpose: Introduces how A/R configuration ties to payments — how terms set due dates and discounts, and how account labels map invoice lines to revenue GL accounts.
scr_ar_about_accounts_receivable_and_pay.outcome: Users understand which setup controls due dates and revenue coding.
scr_ar_about_accounts_receivable_and_pay.rootCause: When aging buckets or revenue coding look wrong, the cause is usually in terms or labels; knowing the linkage speeds diagnosis and prevents fixing symptoms transaction by transaction.
scr_ar_about_accounts_receivable_and_pay.ifSkipped: Users correct individual invoices repeatedly instead of fixing the setup cause.
redFlags: Recurring manual recoding of invoice lines

scr_ar_configuring_a_r_payments.purpose: Configures A/R payment settings — default deposit account, undeposited-funds handling, overpayment treatment and payment methods accepted.
scr_ar_configuring_a_r_payments.outcome: Customer receipts flow to the correct cash and clearing accounts.
scr_ar_configuring_a_r_payments.rootCause: Payment configuration decides whether receipts go straight to operating cash or through 1130 Undeposited Funds; a wrong default breaks deposit matching and the bank reconciliation for every property.
scr_ar_configuring_a_r_payments.ifSkipped: Receipts hit the wrong cash account and bank recs carry unexplained differences.
redFlags: Receipts defaulting to operating cash while deposits run through undeposited funds

scr_ar_adding_an_a_r_term.purpose: Adds an A/R payment term (e.g., Net 30, Due on Receipt, 2/10 Net 30) that sets invoice due dates and early-payment discounts, available to all entities or one.
scr_ar_adding_an_a_r_term.outcome: Consistent due dates and discounts applied to customer invoices.
scr_ar_adding_an_a_r_term.rootCause: Aging buckets and late-fee eligibility are measured from the due date; terms set incorrectly move invoices between buckets and change both collection priorities and the ASC 326 reserve.
scr_ar_adding_an_a_r_term.ifSkipped: Due dates are wrong, aging is misstated and late fees are charged too early or too late.
redFlags: Discount terms on rent invoices
Terms longer than lease payment clauses allow

scr_ar_adding_account_labels.purpose: Adds A/R account labels — friendly names such as 'CAM Recovery' or 'Parking' mapped to specific revenue GL accounts — for use on invoice lines.
scr_ar_adding_account_labels.outcome: Invoice lines post to the correct revenue accounts without users knowing account numbers.
scr_ar_adding_account_labels.rootCause: Site and offshore staff billing charges should not choose raw GL numbers; labels constrain choices to the right revenue accounts and keep recovery income separate from base rent.
scr_ar_adding_account_labels.ifSkipped: Charges are coded to wrong revenue accounts, distorting NOI lines and CAM reconciliations.
redFlags: Labels mapped to balance sheet accounts
Duplicate labels pointing to different accounts

scr_ar_configuration.purpose: Chapter on configuring A/R features — segments, functionality toggles, accounting settings, document sequencing, GL overrides and intercompany bill-backs.
scr_ar_configuration.outcome: A/R configured to match the company's accounting policies.
scr_ar_configuration.rootCause: A/R configuration is set once but affects every invoice and receipt thereafter; a deliberate, documented setup avoids systemic misstatements that are expensive to unwind later.
scr_ar_configuration.ifSkipped: Settings drift from policy and systematic posting errors accumulate.
redFlags: Configuration changes without change-management approval

scr_ar_segments_overview.purpose: Explains segments — custom reporting tags (for example building, unit type or fund) that can be added to A/R transactions beyond the standard entity and account dimensions.
scr_ar_segments_overview.outcome: Receivables and revenue can be reported by attributes the owner cares about.
scr_ar_segments_overview.rootCause: Institutional owners ask for revenue and delinquency by building or fund; segments capture that at transaction time instead of relying on offline spreadsheets.
scr_ar_segments_overview.ifSkipped: Owner-requested segment reporting has to be rebuilt manually every month.
redFlags: Segments added mid-year with no backfill

scr_ar_enabling_segments.purpose: Enables segments in General Ledger configuration so A/R and other applications can tag transactions with them.
scr_ar_enabling_segments.outcome: Segment fields available on A/R invoices and receipts.
scr_ar_enabling_segments.rootCause: Segments must be switched on centrally before any transaction can carry them; enabling late leaves earlier periods untagged and breaks year-over-year comparisons.
scr_ar_enabling_segments.ifSkipped: Segment reports show gaps for periods before enablement.
redFlags: Segments enabled after the fiscal year started

scr_ar_configuring_a_r_functionality.purpose: Turns A/R features on or off — recurring invoices, penalties, statements, deposits, advances — to match how the company bills customers.
scr_ar_configuring_a_r_functionality.outcome: Only the A/R features the company uses are active.
scr_ar_configuring_a_r_functionality.rootCause: Features left off (e.g., penalties or advances) force workarounds such as manual journal entries, which bypass the subledger and break the A/R-to-GL tie-out.
scr_ar_configuring_a_r_functionality.ifSkipped: Needed features are missing and staff post workarounds outside the subledger.
redFlags: Manual JEs to A/R control account because a feature is disabled

scr_ar_configuring_a_r_accounting_settin.purpose: Sets A/R accounting defaults — the A/R control account, advances (prepaid rent) liability account, write-off account and overpayment handling.
scr_ar_configuring_a_r_accounting_settin.outcome: Every A/R posting lands on the correct control and liability accounts.
scr_ar_configuring_a_r_accounting_settin.rootCause: The subledger only reconciles to the GL if all A/R activity posts to one control account; wrong defaults scatter receivables across accounts and break the monthly A/R-to-GL reconciliation.
scr_ar_configuring_a_r_accounting_settin.ifSkipped: The aging no longer ties to 1210 and prepaid rent is misclassified.
redFlags: Two different A/R control accounts in use
Advances posting to revenue

scr_ar_configuring_a_r_document_sequenci.purpose: Configures automatic numbering for A/R documents — invoices, adjustments, receipts — so each has a unique sequential number.
scr_ar_configuring_a_r_document_sequenci.outcome: Gapless, unique document numbers for audit trails.
scr_ar_configuring_a_r_document_sequenci.rootCause: Auditors test completeness by looking for gaps and duplicates in invoice sequences; manual numbering makes that test impossible and invites duplicate billing.
scr_ar_configuring_a_r_document_sequenci.ifSkipped: Duplicate or missing invoice numbers undermine completeness testing.
redFlags: Manual invoice numbering allowed
Sequence resets mid-year

scr_ar_overriding_the_g_l_account_in_a_r.purpose: Explains when and how a user can override the default GL account on an A/R transaction line — for example coding a one-off insurance recovery to a non-standard account.
scr_ar_overriding_the_g_l_account_in_a_r.outcome: Legitimate exceptions coded correctly without changing defaults.
scr_ar_overriding_the_g_l_account_in_a_r.rootCause: Overrides are necessary for unusual charges but also the main route to misposting; controlling who can override and reviewing overrides keeps revenue classification reliable.
scr_ar_overriding_the_g_l_account_in_a_r.ifSkipped: Uncontrolled overrides misclassify revenue and distort NOI lines.
redFlags: Frequent overrides by a single user
Overrides to balance sheet accounts

scr_ar_configuring_intercompany_bill_bac.purpose: Overview of setting up intercompany bill-backs — where one entity pays a shared cost and bills other entities, creating matching A/R and A/P between them.
scr_ar_configuring_intercompany_bill_bac.outcome: Shared costs recovered from sister entities with matching intercompany balances.
scr_ar_configuring_intercompany_bill_bac.rootCause: Shared payroll, insurance and software are often paid by one entity; without formal bill-backs, costs sit in the wrong property's P&L and intercompany balances do not eliminate on consolidation.
scr_ar_configuring_intercompany_bill_bac.ifSkipped: Shared costs stay with the paying entity and intercompany accounts do not net to zero.
redFlags: Due From and Due To balances that do not mirror

scr_ar_enabling_the_intercompany_bill_ba.purpose: Enables the intercompany bill-back subscription in Company setup, a prerequisite before bill-back templates and transactions can be used.
scr_ar_enabling_the_intercompany_bill_ba.outcome: The bill-back feature available to authorised users.
scr_ar_enabling_the_intercompany_bill_ba.rootCause: Bill-backs are an optional subscription; until it is enabled, staff resort to manual intercompany journal entries that are harder to reconcile and eliminate.
scr_ar_enabling_the_intercompany_bill_ba.ifSkipped: Intercompany charges are posted by manual JEs with no matching A/R and A/P.
redFlags: Manual intercompany JEs after the feature is available

scr_ar_granting_permissions_to_bill_back.purpose: Grants users or roles permission to use bill-back templates, restricting who can create intercompany charges between entities.
scr_ar_granting_permissions_to_bill_back.outcome: Only authorised staff can move costs between entities.
scr_ar_granting_permissions_to_bill_back.rootCause: Bill-backs shift expenses between ownership groups; unrestricted access lets costs be moved to entities with different investors, a related-party and fiduciary risk.
scr_ar_granting_permissions_to_bill_back.ifSkipped: Anyone can shift costs between owners, creating disputes and fiduciary exposure.
redFlags: Site-level users with bill-back rights

scr_ar_create_vendors_and_customers_for_.purpose: Creates the vendor and customer records that represent each entity in a bill-back pair — the billing entity as a vendor and the billed entity as a customer.
scr_ar_create_vendors_and_customers_for_.outcome: Each entity can be billed and paid through normal A/R and A/P.
scr_ar_create_vendors_and_customers_for_.rootCause: Bill-backs generate a real invoice and bill; without dedicated intercompany vendor and customer records they post against outside parties and cannot be eliminated.
scr_ar_create_vendors_and_customers_for_.ifSkipped: Intercompany charges mix with third-party balances and eliminations fail.
redFlags: Intercompany customers without an intercompany flag

scr_ar_associating_a_vendor_and_customer.purpose: Links the intercompany vendor and customer records to their entity on the entity record so bill-backs route automatically between the right books.
scr_ar_associating_a_vendor_and_customer.outcome: Bill-backs create the matching bill in the correct receiving entity.
scr_ar_associating_a_vendor_and_customer.rootCause: The association tells RealPage which entity a customer or vendor represents; missing links mean the matching payable is never created on the other side.
scr_ar_associating_a_vendor_and_customer.ifSkipped: One side of the bill-back posts and the intercompany balance never mirrors.
redFlags: Entities missing vendor/customer association

scr_ar_creating_bill_back_templates.purpose: Creates bill-back templates that define which expense and revenue accounts are used when one entity bills another — for example shared payroll billed as a management charge.
scr_ar_creating_bill_back_templates.outcome: Intercompany charges coded consistently on both sides.
scr_ar_creating_bill_back_templates.rootCause: Templates fix the account mapping so the billing entity records a recovery and the billed entity an expense in agreed accounts, rather than users choosing different accounts each time.
scr_ar_creating_bill_back_templates.ifSkipped: Each bill-back is coded differently and property P&Ls are inconsistent.
redFlags: Templates mapping to revenue on the billed side

scr_ar_territories.purpose: Optional territories (e.g., regions or portfolios) that can be assigned to customers for grouping in reports and assigning collection responsibility.
scr_ar_territories.outcome: Customers grouped for regional reporting and collections ownership.
scr_ar_territories.rootCause: Regional managers are accountable for delinquency in their area; territories let aging and collection reports be cut by region without spreadsheets.
scr_ar_territories.ifSkipped: Regional delinquency cannot be reported or assigned cleanly.
redFlags: Customers without a territory

scr_ar_reports.purpose: Chapter overview of A/R reports — aging, customer ledgers, invoice and receipt registers, and segment activity — used in close and collections.
scr_ar_reports.outcome: Users know which A/R report answers which close or collections question.
scr_ar_reports.rootCause: Close reviewers and owners rely on specific A/R reports (aging tie-out, delinquency, receipt registers); knowing them avoids ad-hoc exports that do not tie to the GL.
scr_ar_reports.ifSkipped: Staff build unreconciled spreadsheets instead of using tie-able reports.
redFlags: Owner packages built from exports rather than standard reports

scr_ar_list_of_standard_accounts_receiva.purpose: Lists the standard A/R reports available — aging, customer ledger, invoice register, receipt register, deposit detail — with what each shows.
scr_ar_list_of_standard_accounts_receiva.outcome: The right standard report chosen for each close and review task.
scr_ar_list_of_standard_accounts_receiva.rootCause: Standard reports are tied to the subledger and reproducible; relying on them makes month-end tie-outs repeatable and auditable.
scr_ar_list_of_standard_accounts_receiva.ifSkipped: Custom exports are used and results cannot be reproduced for audit.
redFlags: Aging run at a date other than month-end for tie-out

scr_ar_segment_activity_report.purpose: The Segment Activity report in Financial Analytics, showing GL activity by segment (e.g., building or fund) for A/R revenue and receivables.
scr_ar_segment_activity_report.outcome: Revenue and receivables reported by owner-defined segment.
scr_ar_segment_activity_report.rootCause: Owners with multiple buildings or funds in one entity need results by segment; this report provides it from posted data instead of manual allocation.
scr_ar_segment_activity_report.ifSkipped: Segment results are estimated offline and may not tie to the GL.
redFlags: Segment totals not equal to entity totals

scr_ar_customizing_and_running_the_segme.purpose: Customizes and runs the Segment Activity report — choosing segments, accounts, periods and columns — to answer a specific owner or asset manager question.
scr_ar_customizing_and_running_the_segme.outcome: A tailored segment report that still ties to posted GL activity.
scr_ar_customizing_and_running_the_segme.rootCause: Asset managers ask different questions each month; customizing a GL-tied report beats building one-off spreadsheets that drift from the books.
scr_ar_customizing_and_running_the_segme.ifSkipped: One-off spreadsheets answer owner questions with numbers that do not tie.
redFlags: Saved versions filtering out untagged transactions

scr_ar_segment_activity_columns.purpose: Defines the columns available on the Segment Activity report — beginning balance, debits, credits, net change, ending balance by segment.
scr_ar_segment_activity_columns.outcome: Users read segment activity figures correctly.
scr_ar_segment_activity_columns.rootCause: Misreading net change as ending balance (or vice versa) leads to wrong owner commentary; clear column definitions prevent that.
scr_ar_segment_activity_columns.ifSkipped: Segment figures are misinterpreted in owner reporting.
redFlags: Commentary citing activity columns as balances

scr_ar_about_dimensions.purpose: Explains dimensions — categories such as entity, location, department, customer or segment — used to slice A/R reports and financial statements.
scr_ar_about_dimensions.outcome: Users understand how to cut A/R data by the dimensions that exist.
scr_ar_about_dimensions.rootCause: Every report filter relies on dimensions being populated consistently; understanding them explains why some transactions drop out of a filtered report.
scr_ar_about_dimensions.ifSkipped: Filtered reports silently exclude transactions missing a dimension value.
redFlags: Transactions missing location or department values

scr_ar_limiting_members_in_dimension_str.purpose: Limits which members of a dimension structure appear in reports — for example showing only the properties in one owner's portfolio.
scr_ar_limiting_members_in_dimension_str.outcome: Reports scoped exactly to the owner or region being reviewed.
scr_ar_limiting_members_in_dimension_str.rootCause: Owner reports must not include properties the owner does not own; limiting dimension members enforces that scope and protects confidentiality.
scr_ar_limiting_members_in_dimension_str.ifSkipped: Owner reports include other owners' properties, a confidentiality breach.
redFlags: Portfolio structures not updated after dispositions

scr_ar_attachments.purpose: Chapter on attaching supporting documents — leases, CAM calculations, correspondence, check images — to A/R records.
scr_ar_attachments.outcome: Evidence stored with the transactions it supports.
scr_ar_attachments.rootCause: Auditors and owners ask for support behind invoices, credits and write-offs; keeping it attached to the record avoids hunting through shared drives at audit time.
scr_ar_attachments.ifSkipped: Support for credits and write-offs cannot be produced when auditors request it.
redFlags: Write-offs with no attachment

scr_ar_attachments_overview.purpose: Overview of how RealPage stores attachments centrally and links them to A/R records such as customers, invoices and adjustments.
scr_ar_attachments_overview.outcome: Users understand one document can support several records.
scr_ar_attachments_overview.rootCause: A single lease or settlement letter can support multiple invoices and credits; central storage avoids duplicate uploads and conflicting versions.
scr_ar_attachments_overview.ifSkipped: Documents are uploaded repeatedly and versions conflict.
redFlags: Several versions of the same lease attached

scr_ar_adding_an_attachment_to_the_syste.purpose: Uploads a new attachment into Company storage so it can be linked to A/R records later — for example a signed lease amendment.
scr_ar_adding_an_attachment_to_the_syste.outcome: A document stored and ready to link.
scr_ar_adding_an_attachment_to_the_syste.rootCause: Uploading once to central storage with a clear name and folder makes support retrievable by anyone reviewing the account, not only the person who received it.
scr_ar_adding_an_attachment_to_the_syste.ifSkipped: Support lives in personal inboxes and is lost when staff change.
redFlags: Attachments with generic names like 'scan1.pdf'

scr_ar_adding_a_new_attachment_to_a_reco.purpose: Uploads and links a new attachment directly to an A/R record, such as attaching the tenant's approval email to a rent concession credit.
scr_ar_adding_a_new_attachment_to_a_reco.outcome: The transaction and its evidence stored together.
scr_ar_adding_a_new_attachment_to_a_reco.rootCause: Credits and concessions reduce revenue and are high-risk; attaching approval at the time of entry is the simplest evidence of authorization.
scr_ar_adding_a_new_attachment_to_a_reco.ifSkipped: Concessions cannot be proven as approved during audit.
redFlags: Credits over threshold with no attachment

scr_ar_adding_an_existing_attachment_to_.purpose: Links an attachment already in storage to another A/R record — for example linking one lease to several recurring invoices.
scr_ar_adding_an_existing_attachment_to_.outcome: Shared support linked without duplicate uploads.
scr_ar_adding_an_existing_attachment_to_.rootCause: Reusing the stored document keeps one authoritative version across related records and saves storage and review time.
scr_ar_adding_an_existing_attachment_to_.ifSkipped: Duplicate uploads create conflicting versions of support.
redFlags: Superseded lease versions linked to current invoices

scr_ar_viewing_an_attachment.purpose: Opens an attachment from Company storage and shows every A/R record it supports, such as the lease behind several recurring invoices.
scr_ar_viewing_an_attachment.outcome: Quick access to support for review and audit requests.
scr_ar_viewing_an_attachment.rootCause: Reviewers and auditors need to open support on demand during PBC fieldwork; direct viewing avoids emailing documents around.
scr_ar_viewing_an_attachment.ifSkipped: Audit requests take longer as documents are hunted down.
redFlags: Attachments that fail to open or are corrupted

scr_ar_editing_an_attachment.purpose: Edits an attachment's name, description or folder in Company storage to keep support organized and searchable.
scr_ar_editing_an_attachment.outcome: Attachments named and filed so they can be found later.
scr_ar_editing_an_attachment.rootCause: Consistent naming (property, customer, document type, date) is what makes support searchable years later during audits or disputes.
scr_ar_editing_an_attachment.ifSkipped: Support exists but cannot be located when needed.
redFlags: Renaming attachments to obscure their content

scr_ar_deleting_or_removing_an_attachmen.purpose: Removes an attachment from a record or deletes it from storage when it was attached in error.
scr_ar_deleting_or_removing_an_attachmen.outcome: Wrong documents no longer mislead reviewers.
scr_ar_deleting_or_removing_an_attachmen.rootCause: Wrongly attached documents (another tenant's lease) mislead reviewers and may expose personal data; removal must be controlled so real support is not destroyed.
scr_ar_deleting_or_removing_an_attachmen.ifSkipped: Misattached documents mislead reviewers or expose other customers' data.
redFlags: Deletion of support for write-offs or credits

scr_ar_miscellaneous_common_tasks.purpose: Chapter on everyday A/R housekeeping — naming conventions, default line values, managing lists and views, exporting, audit trails and terminology.
scr_ar_miscellaneous_common_tasks.outcome: Consistent everyday use of A/R across the offshore team.
scr_ar_miscellaneous_common_tasks.rootCause: Small inconsistencies (IDs, list filters, views) compound across thousands of customers; shared conventions keep data clean and reviews efficient.
scr_ar_miscellaneous_common_tasks.ifSkipped: Data conventions drift and reviewers waste time interpreting inconsistent records.
redFlags: No documented naming convention

scr_ar_about_this_chapter.purpose: Introduces the miscellaneous common tasks chapter and the housekeeping procedures it covers for A/R users.
scr_ar_about_this_chapter.outcome: Users know where to find routine A/R housekeeping guidance.
scr_ar_about_this_chapter.rootCause: Housekeeping tasks are learned informally and inconsistently; a clear pointer to the reference reduces variation between offshore team members.
scr_ar_about_this_chapter.ifSkipped: Each user follows their own habits and records become inconsistent.
redFlags: Training materials not referencing standard procedures

scr_ar_best_practices_for_creating_names.purpose: Best practices for customer and record IDs — stable, unique, meaningful codes (e.g., property code + tenant suite) that never get reused.
scr_ar_best_practices_for_creating_names.outcome: Customer IDs that stay unique and traceable across years.
scr_ar_best_practices_for_creating_names.rootCause: Customer IDs link invoices, receipts and history; reused or ad-hoc IDs merge different tenants' histories and corrupt collections and audit trails.
scr_ar_best_practices_for_creating_names.ifSkipped: Two tenants share an ID history and balances are misattributed.
redFlags: IDs reused after a tenant moves out

scr_ar_setting_default_line_item_values.purpose: Sets default values (account label, location, department) that pre-fill new A/R invoice lines to reduce keying and miscoding.
scr_ar_setting_default_line_item_values.outcome: Faster, more consistent invoice line coding.
scr_ar_setting_default_line_item_values.rootCause: Defaults reduce errors on repetitive billing but also propagate a wrong code everywhere if set incorrectly, so they must be chosen and reviewed deliberately.
scr_ar_setting_default_line_item_values.ifSkipped: Users key codes manually each time and coding varies.
redFlags: Default location set to the wrong property

scr_ar_managing_lists.purpose: How to work with A/R list pages — customers, invoices, receipts — using sort, filter, views and export to find records quickly.
scr_ar_managing_lists.outcome: Efficient location of the records needed for reviews and collections.
scr_ar_managing_lists.rootCause: Collections and close reviews start from lists; efficient list use cuts time finding overdue invoices or unapplied receipts.
scr_ar_managing_lists.ifSkipped: Reviews are slower and exceptions are missed in long lists.
redFlags: Persistent filters hiding records

scr_ar_sorting_lists.purpose: Sorts A/R lists by column — for example invoices by due date or amount — to prioritise collections and reviews.
scr_ar_sorting_lists.outcome: The oldest or largest items surfaced first.
scr_ar_sorting_lists.rootCause: Collections effort is best spent on the largest and oldest balances; sorting surfaces them immediately.
scr_ar_sorting_lists.ifSkipped: Collectors work alphabetically and large overdue balances wait.
redFlags: Largest items not reviewed first

scr_ar_filtering_lists.purpose: Uses column filters on A/R lists to narrow records — for example open invoices over 90 days for one property.
scr_ar_filtering_lists.outcome: A focused list of the records that need action.
scr_ar_filtering_lists.rootCause: Portfolios hold thousands of invoices; filters isolate the exceptions a reviewer or collector must act on.
scr_ar_filtering_lists.ifSkipped: Exceptions are lost among routine records.
redFlags: Filters left on that hide exceptions from later users

scr_ar_examples_of_using_filters_with_fi.purpose: Worked examples of filter syntax — ranges, wildcards, blanks — for A/R fields like amount, date and customer name.
scr_ar_examples_of_using_filters_with_fi.outcome: Users build precise filters for exception review.
scr_ar_examples_of_using_filters_with_fi.rootCause: Imprecise filters (e.g., missing blanks) exclude records silently; examples teach filters that capture every exception.
scr_ar_examples_of_using_filters_with_fi.ifSkipped: Filters miss records and reviews are incomplete.
redFlags: Filters excluding blank values unintentionally

scr_ar_list_views.purpose: Explains list views — saved combinations of columns, sorts and filters — used for recurring A/R reviews such as 'unapplied receipts'.
scr_ar_list_views.outcome: Recurring reviews run from the same view each month.
scr_ar_list_views.rootCause: Using the same saved view each month makes reviews repeatable and comparable, which reviewers and auditors rely on.
scr_ar_list_views.ifSkipped: Each month's review uses different criteria and exceptions slip through.
redFlags: Review views edited without notice

scr_ar_drop_down_list_controls.purpose: Explains drop-down controls on A/R forms — searching, selecting and adding values such as customers or account labels inline.
scr_ar_drop_down_list_controls.outcome: Correct values selected quickly on A/R forms.
scr_ar_drop_down_list_controls.rootCause: Inline 'add new' in drop-downs can create duplicate customers or labels; knowing the controls prevents accidental master data creation.
scr_ar_drop_down_list_controls.ifSkipped: Duplicate customers and labels are created from forms.
redFlags: Customers created via drop-down with incomplete data

scr_ar_custom_list_views.purpose: Explains custom list views that users create for their own A/R work — for example a collections view showing balance, last payment and contact.
scr_ar_custom_list_views.outcome: Views tailored to each person's A/R tasks.
scr_ar_custom_list_views.rootCause: Standard views rarely show everything needed for collections calls; custom views bring the relevant fields together.
scr_ar_custom_list_views.ifSkipped: Users export to spreadsheets to see needed fields together.
redFlags: Shared views changed by individuals

scr_ar_adding_a_new_custom_view.purpose: Creates and saves a new custom A/R list view with chosen columns, filters and sort order, optionally shared with the team.
scr_ar_adding_a_new_custom_view.outcome: A reusable view available to the team.
scr_ar_adding_a_new_custom_view.rootCause: A shared custom view standardises how the team reviews open items, so every property is checked the same way.
scr_ar_adding_a_new_custom_view.ifSkipped: Review criteria differ between team members.
redFlags: Team views owned by departed users

scr_ar_exporting_lists.purpose: Exports an A/R list to CSV or Excel for analysis, collections work or evidence packages.
scr_ar_exporting_lists.outcome: A/R data available for offline analysis.
scr_ar_exporting_lists.rootCause: Exports are often needed for owner questions or audits, but they leave the system; they must be tied back to reports and handled securely.
scr_ar_exporting_lists.ifSkipped: Analysis is manual; or exports circulate without tying to the GL.
redFlags: Exports containing resident personal data emailed externally

scr_ar_audit_trails.purpose: Explains A/R audit trails — the log of who created, edited, posted or deleted each record and when.
scr_ar_audit_trails.outcome: Every change to receivables is traceable to a user and time.
scr_ar_audit_trails.rootCause: Auditors and owners rely on audit trails to test that credits, write-offs and edits were made by authorized people; without them, fraud and error cannot be investigated.
scr_ar_audit_trails.ifSkipped: Unauthorized changes to receivables cannot be traced.
redFlags: Edits to posted invoices by users without that role

scr_ar_viewing_audit_trails.purpose: Views a record's audit trail — each action, field changed, old and new values, user and time.
scr_ar_viewing_audit_trails.outcome: Investigation of who changed what on a receivable.
scr_ar_viewing_audit_trails.rootCause: When a customer disputes a balance or a credit appears unexpectedly, the audit trail is the first evidence to establish what happened.
scr_ar_viewing_audit_trails.ifSkipped: Disputes and anomalies cannot be investigated with evidence.
redFlags: Changes made outside business hours

scr_ar_exporting_a_records_audit_trail.purpose: Exports a record's audit trail for audit evidence, investigations or dispute files.
scr_ar_exporting_a_records_audit_trail.rootCause: Auditors and legal counsel need audit history outside the system; exporting preserves it as evidence.
scr_ar_exporting_a_records_audit_trail.ifSkipped: Evidence cannot be provided to auditors or counsel.
redFlags: Audit trails requested but not exported

scr_ar_terminology_list.purpose: Shows the Terminology page listing system terms that can be renamed — for example renaming 'Customer' to 'Tenant' or 'Location' to 'Property'.
scr_ar_terminology_list.outcome: Screens use the vocabulary the company uses.
scr_ar_terminology_list.rootCause: Property managers think in tenants and properties; matching terminology reduces confusion and training time for site and offshore staff.
scr_ar_terminology_list.ifSkipped: Generic terms confuse users and mismatch owner reporting.
redFlags: Renamed terms not reflected in training material

scr_ar_changing_a_realpage_accounting_te.purpose: Changes a system term — for example renaming 'Location' to 'Property' — across all screens and reports.
scr_ar_changing_a_realpage_accounting_te.outcome: Consistent company-specific terms on screens and reports.
scr_ar_changing_a_realpage_accounting_te.rootCause: Term changes appear on owner-facing reports too; changing deliberately avoids confusing labels in financial packages.
scr_ar_changing_a_realpage_accounting_te.ifSkipped: Terms are inconsistent across reports and screens.
redFlags: Term changes that make reports ambiguous

scr_ar_roles_and_permissions.purpose: Explains roles and permissions for A/R — who can create invoices, post credits, apply receipts, write off balances and change setup.
scr_ar_roles_and_permissions.outcome: A/R access aligned to job duties with segregation of duties.
scr_ar_roles_and_permissions.rootCause: The same person billing, receiving cash and writing off balances can conceal misappropriation (lapping); roles enforce segregation required by SOC 1 and owner agreements.
scr_ar_roles_and_permissions.ifSkipped: One user can post cash and write off the related receivable, enabling concealed theft.
redFlags: Users with both receipt and write-off rights

scr_ar_duplicating_records.purpose: Creates a new record (such as a role or customer) by duplicating an existing one and changing only what differs.
scr_ar_duplicating_records.rootCause: Duplicating speeds setup but copies every attribute, including permissions or tax settings that may be wrong for the new record; each copy needs review.
scr_ar_duplicating_records.ifSkipped: Similar records are keyed from scratch with inconsistencies.
redFlags: Roles duplicated from administrator roles

scr_ar_adding_a_g_l_account.purpose: Adds a GL account needed for A/R — for example a new revenue account for EV-charging income — and assigns chart types.
scr_ar_adding_a_g_l_account.outcome: New revenue or receivable accounts available for A/R coding.
scr_ar_adding_a_g_l_account.rootCause: New income streams need their own account so they appear separately in the income statement and owner reports rather than being buried in other income.
scr_ar_adding_a_g_l_account.ifSkipped: New revenue is buried in generic accounts and owner reporting lacks detail.
redFlags: Accounts added without mapping to owner reporting

scr_ar_adding_a_contact.purpose: Adds a contact record (name, email, phone, address) that can be linked to customers as billing or statement contacts.
scr_ar_adding_a_contact.outcome: Correct people receive invoices and statements.
scr_ar_adding_a_contact.rootCause: Invoices and statements are delivered to contacts; accurate contacts are what make billing reach the person who pays.
scr_ar_adding_a_contact.ifSkipped: Invoices go nowhere and collections are delayed.
redFlags: Contacts with no email for emailed statements
